text:
Joel Hofer was the difference. He stopped all 25 shots St. Louis faced on a night when the Blues were expected to give up 2.89 goals, which means he erased nearly three goals' worth of Dallas chances by himself. Oettinger, by contrast, stopped 20 of 22 against 2.4 expected and was roughly average. The Blues won 4-0 at American Airlines Center, but the way the game was played says Dallas deserved to win it 59 percent of the time.

The Stars had 59 shot attempts to 50 and owned the second period, where they generated 1.37 expected goals to 0.23 for St. Louis. Dalibor Dvorsky still scored in that period at 13:05 on a snap shot rated at just a 17 percent chance, the kind of finish that tilts a game the other team was controlling. Mason McTavish had opened the scoring 1:34 into the first on a snap shot off feeds from Colton Parayko and Jimmy Snuggerud. Neither team scored on the power play, Dallas going 0 for 4 and St. Louis 0 for 4.

The score only became lopsided at the end. Snuggerud, who finished with 0.94 individual expected goals, wrist-shot one in at 17:37 of the third on a 69 percent chance. Fifteen seconds later, Pius Suter made it 4-0 off a pass from Hofer, the goalie, who picked up an assist on top of his shutout. Two goals in 15 seconds turned a game Dallas had mostly played well into a rout on the scoreboard.
